goal: Create a substantive, source-bound educational draft about Intel 8086 and its relation to 8088; do not merely paraphrase ten definitions.

source_documents.locator: At a Glance; paragraphs on 1978 and IBM PC
facts: The original IBM PC model 5150 used the 8088, a variant of the 8086, rather than an 8086 processor.
The IBM PC launched in August 1981.
8086 has 16-bit registers and a 16-bit external data bus.
8088 has an 8-bit external data bus but is otherwise similar to the 8086.
Segmentation uses 16-bit segment registers and up to 64-KByte segments; 8086/8088 have four segment registers active at a time.

source_documents.locator: Chapter 2, Segmentation and Physical Address Generation, printed pages 2-11 to 2-13
facts: The original Intel manual describes 20-bit physical addresses from 00000H to FFFFFH.
Physical address is generated by shifting the 16-bit segment value left four bit positions and adding a 16-bit offset.
Segments begin on 16-byte boundaries and may overlap.
